title: Post-Operative Visual Decline: The 4-Week Post-Cataract Crisis
summary: Visual decline four weeks post-cataract surgery is a complex diagnostic challenge requiring immediate differentiation between infectious, inflammatory, and structural etiologies. This guide provides a systematic clinical framework for the evaluation and management of delayed-onset visual loss.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Referral Needed
content: IOP > 30 mmHg unresponsive to topical therapy

sections.title: Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) Diagnostic Protocol
content: Step 1: Perform dilated fundoscopy to assess macular contour.
Step 2: Obtain Spectral-Domain OCT (look for intraretinal fluid pockets).
Step 3: Consider FFA (Fundus Fluorescein Angiography) for late-phase petaloid staining.
Step 4: Initiate topical NSAIDs (Bromfenac 0.09% or Nepafenac 0.3%) + topical steroids.

sections.title: P. acnes Endophthalmitis: Clinical Pearls
content: Classic 'White Plaque' located in the lens capsular bag.
Requires pars plana vitrectomy with capsular bag lavage.
Intravitreal vancomycin is the gold standard treatment.

sections.title: Mnemonic: Why is the vision dropping?

content.explanation: C: Cystoid Macular Edema, L: Lens/Capsule (PCO/IOL tilt), E: Endophthalmitis (Delayed), A: Ametropia (Residual refractive error), R: Retinal (RD or ERM).

sections.title: Management of PCO
sections.content: Nd:YAG laser capsulotomy is the definitive treatment for symptomatic PCO. Ensure the IOL is stable and no active inflammation is present. Typical energy levels: 0.8–2.0 mJ per shot. Complications include IOL pitting, transient IOP spikes, and retinal detachment (rare). Check IOP 1 hour post-procedure.
